Subject: PrivGPU connectivity & capacity: concurrency profile, egress staging, sprint actions

Alex / Nina —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. We sketched a pragmatic plan during the call to move SummitAI's private deployment from proof-of-concept to a steady-state 99th%-latency-backed offering. Before we lock sprint tasks, I need two quick clarifications so our capacity runbook is accurate:

1) Concurrency distribution: the traffic you described has a heavy head (short chat bursts) and a long tail (batch reranks). Can you attach a percentile breakdown for 1m/5m/1h windows? I attached summitai-concurrency-profiles.csv as a working template — please populate if you can.

2) Egress & peering: your datacenter team mentioned an NVA firewall in front of the egress path. What are the sustained/peak egress throughput caps we should assume per availability zone? We need these numbers to size crossconnects and to declare warm-pool headroom.

Proposed capacity targets (from Redwood ops):
- Throughput SLO: 20k tokens/s sustained, 35k tokens/s 5-min burst 
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 180ms for interactive routes (max seq 1024)
- Initial headroom: 35% above expected steady-state QPS for first 30 days

Attachments: egress-topology-sketch.png (network arrows), sprint-MAP-v1.docx (proposed mutual action plan).

I'd like to run a 60-minute sync tomorrow to finalize the MCP and the sprint owners. Proposed time: Tue 06/30 10:00 PT.

Goal for sync: agree on concurrency percentiles, egress caps, warm-pool size and autoscale ramp windows so we can commit a GPU count for the first delivery.

Thanks —
Grace
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- We'll fill the CSV today with per-route percentiles. Expect high spikeiness from the assisted-chat route (p50 ~ 3 req/s, p99 ~ 48 req/s for heavy users during peak). Rerank flows are batched (p95 latency tolerant).
- Our colo team (ops@datacenterpartners.io) limits public egress per AZ to 8 Gbps sustained and they allow short bursts to 12 Gbps with explicit traffic shaping. The NVA adds ~1.2ms processing on the egress path under normal load.

We can make time for 10:00 PT tomorrow. I'll ask ops to join for the peering bit.

Adding the internal telemetry perspective — I pulled a quick sample from similar customers to give baseline numbers we should assume if SummitAI doesn't produce a filled CSV by EOD: 

Observed concurrency mix (sample customers, seq <=1024):
- interactive-chat: p50 2.7 r/s, p90 12 r/s, p95 28 r/s, p99 46 r/s
- embed+rake: p50 0.2 r/s, p95 6 r/s (batched)
- rerank-batch: median batch size 24, p95 batch latency tolerant (<= 1.2s)

Headroom guidance: start with warm pool equivalent to 25% of worst-case sustained GPU requirement and add 10% per expected ramp event in the first month. Warm pool = GPUs kept with KV cache primed and container warm; target warmup < 45s for typical models via KV prefetch and cold-start kernel caching.

I'll bring a rough spreadsheet to the sync that projects GPU count under 3 scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic).

-Dylan

Notes from model-serving perspective — short bullets: 
- KV cache warmup: for the LLM family we plan to warm top-10 hot prefixes per tenant; warming 10 prefixes reduces p95 token latency by ~18% in our microbench. Warmup cost is ~0.6 tokens/sec equivalent for 1 GPU for 60s.
- Multiplexing: avoid >8 simultaneous tenant multiplexes per GPU for interactive-sensitive routes; multiplexing beyond that causes p95 tail degradation due to KV cache thrash.
- Quantization impact: 4-bit quantized variants show ~8% higher throughput but add variability in tail. Recommend conservative headroom if using mixed Q profiles.

I attached the sprint-MAP-v1.docx with the ops/workflow I recommend: 1) lock routes and SLOs, 2) stage warm-pool + egress shaping test, 3) run soak at 60% expected QPS for 48h, 4) cutover with gradual ramp.

-Irene
Principal Applied ML Engineer

Subject: Re: PrivGPU connectivity & capacity: concurrency profile, egress staging, sprint actions

Quick capacity calc (back-of-envelope) using Alex's egress cap and the suggested SLOs: 
- Assume model throughput 1.6 tokens/ms per A100-equivalent GPU (seq=1024 baseline) => ~62.5k tokens/s per GPU peak in ideal microbench. Realistic steady-state for safety factor 0.35 (model overhead, multiplexing, quantization) => ~40k tokens/s effective per GPU.
- To meet 20k sustained tokens/s with 35% initial headroom => required capacity = 20k * 1.35 / 40k ≈ 0.675 GPUs → round up to 1 GPU baseline per AZ.
- For the 35k 5-min burst target: required = 35k * 1.35 / 40k ≈ 1.18 GPUs → need ability to scale to 2 GPUs per AZ for bursts.

Autoscale implications: our autoscaler has 60–90s spin-up for cold GPUs (driver module + kernel JIT). With warm pools sized as Irene suggests, we can get warm ramp to +1 GPU in ~25–40s. If SummitAI's AZ egress is limited to 8Gbps, we must ensure crossconnects don't saturate at peak token rates (I'll validate token -> bytes mapping with ops).

I'll bring a short slide with the rounding recommendations and a sample ops runbook.

-Markus
Staff Infra Engineer
